items.title: Life insurers thrive on group cover in Oct as retail APE lags
items.description: Life insurance firms in India experienced a noteworthy 26% rise in new business premiums year-over-year for October, thanks mainly to robust group insurance growth. On the other hand, retail annualised premium equivalent only saw a modest uptick of 5.2%, while individual policy sales declined by 3.7%. This scenario points to retail sector hurdles, although the increasing popularity of protection products could signal potential for future expansion.

items.title: Blackstone lines up $200 million loan to refinance ASK credit line
items.description: Blackstone is in the process of arranging a $200 million loan for ASK Investment Managers. This loan aims to refinance an existing sponsor-financing facility that matures in 2027. Four banks are leading this transaction, which is currently being syndicated among international lenders. The refinancing effort reflects private equity investors' strategy to manage acquisition-related debt maturities.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty mark 2-week winning run on FPI inflows
items.description: Indian equity benchmarks in Mumbai have seen a two-week winning streak with significant foreign investment. Foreign Portfolio Investors have invested over ₹75,000 crore in November, while domestic institutional investors have sold shares worth around ₹46,835 crore. The BSE Sensex and NSE Nifty both experienced mild increases despite profit booking by domestic investors. Brent crude oil prices have declined, contributing positively to India's macroeconomic outlook.

items.title: These large-, mid- and small-cap stocks have upside potential of more than 20% in 1 year, according to analysts
items.description: The probability of a sharp, damaging downturn now appears low, and the broad direction favours the market. So, the stance should be the same as in these past few weeks: Shedding fear, but cautiously optimistic. Focus on the business under the stock you are interested in, and keep one eye on what is happening globally.

items.title: Pre-market action: Here's the trade setup for today's session
items.description: Indian equities ended marginally higher as profit booking pared early gains, while small- and micro-cap stocks outperformed largecaps. Analysts attribute the broader market resilience to sustained domestic investor participation and buying interest beyond frontline stocks.

items.title: Stocks in news: Vodafone Idea, M&M, Ola Electric, IRCTC, Oil India and Zee Entertainment
items.description: The Nifty ended marginally higher on Thursday, with analysts identifying 25,000–25,150 as the immediate support zone and 25,400–25,500 as resistance. Meanwhile, Vodafone Idea, M&M, Ola Electric, IRCTC, Oil India and Zee Entertainment are among the stocks likely to remain in focus on Friday amid earnings and company-specific developments.

items.title: DIIs book profits in longest selling streak in 4 years
items.description: Domestic institutional investors have recently unloaded more than ₹47,662 crore worth of equities amidst a market upswing. This shift showcases their tendency to lock in profits following substantial input into Indian stocks. Conversely, foreign portfolio investors have returned vigorously, investing about $8 billion since mid-October. This marks a notable change in market behavior, as local investors experience their longest selling streak in four years.

items.title: MSCI adds LIC, Coforge, Adani Green and Meesho to Emerging Markets Index
items.description: MSCI will include Life Insurance Corporation of India, Coforge, Adani Green Energy, and Meesho in its index. The changes will take effect on November 30, with passive inflows expected for these new additions. PI Industries will be excluded, leading to an estimate of outflows from this stock. Additionally, the overall number of constituents will increase to 168 in the index.

items.title: Stock Radar: Adani Power stock showing signs of recovery after falling 18% from highs; what should investors do?
items.description: Adani Power Ltd has rebounded after testing key support levels, which indicates a positive trend. Analysts suggest that short-term traders could buy the stock with a target of Rs 245. The stock recently experienced a significant decline but remains within an ascending channel. Technical indicators support a bullish outlook for the stock's trajectory moving forward. This analysis highlights potential volatility and the importance of maintaining trend support.

items.title: Smaller MFIs change tack: No onlending, just routing funds
items.description: India’s microfinance sector is seeing a structural shift as funding constraints and mounting stress push smaller lenders away from direct lending towards business correspondent models. With bank funding and fresh equity drying up, lenders are increasingly pursuing off-balance-sheet growth and earning fee income by acting as agents for banks. Industry leaders say the traditional joint-liability group lending model is losing relevance as borrowers gain access to multiple formal and digital credit options.

items.title: NSE International Exchange opens UK, France, 5 more European markets to Indian investors
items.description: NSE International Exchange has expanded its global investment platform to seven European markets, giving Indian investors access to over 11,500 securities, including 8,200-plus UCITS ETFs, through its GIFT City-based entity.

items.title: NSE shares cross Rs 2,000 mark for first time, jump 22% from record low in less than a month. More upside ahead?
items.description: NSE shares surged 22% in around three weeks from their October record low of Rs 1,640 to hit a fresh high of Rs 2,007.60 on Friday, crossing the Rs 2,000 mark for the first time. The stock is now up 11.5% from its listing price and 12.5% from its IPO price.

items.title: MSCI rejig: Which stocks may see the biggest inflows & outflows?
items.description: MSCI announced several additions and exclusion of Indian stocks to its indices, increasing India’s overall weight in the MSCI Emerging Markets Index to 11.7%, which Nuvama believes will lead to passive inflows of around $2 billion. The brokerages listed out which stocks may see the biggest inflows and outflows following the changes that will take effect from November 30 onwards.

items.title: HAL shares range-bound despite better-than-expected Q2 results. What Goldman Sachs, Nuvama and other brokerages expect
items.description: Shares of Hindustan Aeronautics traded mixed after reporting a 16% year-on-year profit increase. Revenue from operations also rose nearly 15%, leading to varied brokerage reactions. Nuvama maintained a 'Hold' rating, citing execution concerns despite a strong order backlog. Both Goldman Sachs and Citi issued 'Buy' ratings, indicating upside potential based on future deliveries. Analysts emphasize the importance of execution and inventory preparedness for sustained growth.

items.title: SpiceJet shares hit 5% upper circuit despite operational challenges. What's behind the surge?
items.description: SpiceJet shares hit the 5% upper circuit after the airline announced a board meeting on November 18 to consider a fresh capital raise. The stock climbed to Rs 8.67 on the BSE, taking its market capitalisation to Rs 1,323 crore. The rally came despite operational challenges and rising crude oil prices weighing on the aviation sector.

items.title: Manappuram Finance shares drop 3% even as Q2 net profit soars 3x to Rs 701 crore. Why did Jefferies cut target price?
items.description: Manappuram Finance shares fell 3% despite reporting a more than threefold jump in Q2 net profit. Jefferies retained its Buy rating but cut the target price to Rs 400, citing growth opportunities, improving margins and potential recovery in return ratios.

items.title: What are retail investors buying? The bets just got bigger in 50 multibaggers that soared up to 1,400%
items.description: Retail investors are actively bolstering their positions in various stocks that have delivered exceptional returns this year. Companies such as Sterlite Technologies and HFCL have witnessed a surge in retail investment alongside notable share price increases. After enduring a slump, the Indian stock market is on the mend, with a marked rise in foreign investments recorded in November.

items.title: Sensex, Nifty's explosive rally pushes market to pre-Middle East war levels. How long will they take to scale fresh peaks?
items.description: In a remarkable turn of events, the Indian stock market has showcased impressive upward movement this month, with the Sensex soaring to 82,000, indicating a robust rebound following the recent conflict. Analysts suggest that if favorable conditions persist, lifetime highs could be on the horizon in the coming months. However, investors are urged to remain vigilant due to potential external volatility, and to consider acquiring top-quality stocks during any downturns.

items.title: 12 bluechip stocks within 5% of their 52-week highs; should you chase them now?
items.description: India's stock market has made a remarkable comeback, emerging as the top global performer thanks to a resurgence in foreign investments. After a challenging phase marked by persistent selling from foreign investors, the re-entry of foreign institutional investors (FIIs) has invigorated market liquidity and boosted investor sentiment. Although there are encouraging signs of earnings recovery, experts warn that profit-booking and various economic factors could pose risks to ongoing growth.

items.title: MSTC shares skyrocket 20% to hit upper circuit. Here’s why
items.description: MSTC shares hit the 20% upper circuit after the state-owned company reported its strongest second-quarter performance since listing, with consolidated profit after tax rising 57.7% YoY to Rs 74.92 crore. Revenue from operations grew 29.4% to Rs 110.02 crore. The stock also gained after receiving in-principle RBI approval to operate a TReDS platform.

items.title: From worst to best! India is now the best performing stock market in the last one month. Missed the rally?
items.description: India's stock market has made a remarkable recovery, proudly standing as the top performer in the world over the past month. This upswing is largely credited to a wave of foreign investments that has bolstered liquidity and confidence among investors. The backing from domestic institutions and a clearer outlook on corporate earnings have also played a role.

items.title: Hitachi Energy India shares jump 8% as brokerages raise targets after Q2 beat
items.description: Hitachi Energy India shares surged after a strong Q2 performance, with revenue rising 64% YoY to Rs 2,997 crore, beating Jefferies’ estimates by 26%. EBITDA grew 36% to Rs 406 crore, while reported profit increased 20% to Rs 319 crore.

items.title: Why is market falling today? Sensex drops 600 points, Nifty below 25,100 as explosive rally hits the brakes. 5 key factors explained
items.description: Indian stock market indices Sensex and Nifty fell after a sustained rally, declining significantly on November 13. The Sensex dropped over 600 points while Nifty traded below the 25,100 level. Major stocks such as M&M and HDFC Bank contributed to the losses, each falling nearly 2%. Broader markets also reported losses, impacting various sectors including Nifty Auto and Nifty Private Bank.

items.title: Vodafone Idea shares fall 3% after Q2 loss widens to Rs 5,975 crore on exceptional charges, ARPU rises to Rs 198
items.description: Vodafone Idea reported a higher Q2 FY27 net loss of ₹5,975 crore, despite 6% revenue growth to ₹11,884 crore. ARPU rose nearly 10% to ₹198, supported by customer upgrades. Subscriber numbers, data usage and EBITDA improved, while capital expenditure more than doubled sequentially amid ongoing network expansion efforts.

items.title: Ola Electric shares sink 6% as Q2 revenue falls 39% YoY. What's next?
items.description: Ola Electric shares fell over 6% after the company reported a 39% YoY decline in September-quarter revenue to Rs 421 crore, despite narrowing its consolidated net loss to Rs 362 crore. Sequentially, losses widened and revenue declined 7.5%. The stock slipped to Rs 33.48 on the NSE as investors weighed the weak revenue performance and profitability trends.

items.title: Aditya Birla Capital among 9 stocks showing White Marubozu Pattern
items.description: On November 12, nine stocks in the Nifty500 that rose over 5.5% appeared on the ‘White Marubozu’ bullish scanner, according to StockEdge’s technical scan data. A White Marubozu is a bullish candlestick pattern in technical analysis that occurs when the opening price is the lowest for a given period, and the closing price is the highest.The pattern is represented by a long white (or green) candlestick with no upper shadow and little or no lower shadow. It reflects strong upward price movement during the session, with the price moving from the opening level toward the session high by the close. The pattern is commonly studied in technical analysis as an indicator of price momentum.
